_schema_notes: Each program: id, name, category[], org_type, agency, benefit, who_its_for, eligibility[], required_documents[], application_process, apply_url, status, confidence, source_url, source_checked, notes. confidence is 'high' (multi-field confirmed on official .gov.ng page) or 'needs_verification' (not yet checked, or official page lacks detail). Never present a 'needs_verification' program in the demo without saying so. access_pathway is one of: self_service_application, registry_gated, automatic_institutional, agency_sponsored, unknown, not_applicable — determines which CTA pattern the card uses (see ClaimAm design findings doc). Bank/lender entries (org_type containing 'bank') additionally carry financing_type ('non_interest_sharia' or 'conventional') and religion_note, since users specifically ask whether Sharia-compliant banks lend to non-Muslims — religion_note states what the source actually confirms per bank, not a blanket claim.

Enrolled at a federal or state-owned university, polytechnic, monotechnic, college of education, or vocational/innovation enterprise institution (IEI)
Active, currently enrolled student (not a graduate or prospective applicant)
Valid NIN required
Institution must have uploaded the student's record to the NELFUND Student Verification Portal

programs.notes: IMPORTANT FIX: the previously recorded apply_url (nelfund.gov.ng) does not resolve (DNS failure) — it is a dead domain, not the real NELFUND site. The correct official domain is nelf.gov.ng, with the application portal at portal.nelf.gov.ng. Anyone who had bookmarked or shared the old .gov.ng-look-alike link should be redirected — this is exactly the kind of stale/wrong link the 'never show a fake Apply now' design principle is meant to catch.

programs.name: NNPC/Chevron JV National Merit Scholarship

programs.benefit: ₦200,000/year, renewable each academic year until graduation (subject to continued eligibility)

Minimum CGPA of 3.5/5.0 (or equivalent)
At least six O'Level credits obtained in one sitting

required_documents: needs_verification for exact list — likely admission letter, O'Level result, current CGPA/transcript, means of ID

programs.status: 2026 cycle applications closed 30 June 2026; reopens annually — recheck before demo
programs.source_url: Aggregator sources (edugist.org, scholarsworld.ng, masteredu.com.ng) converge consistently; the Scholastica platform itself was independently corroborated as the genuine official channel by multiple unrelated sources including explicit anti-scam warnings naming this exact domain ('CNL does NOT assign representatives or agents... avoid look-alike domains')
programs.notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: an initial automated fetch of candidate.scholastica.ng read as a sparse, hard-to-verify site — a second independent search corroborated it as the real shared platform for multiple legitimate oil-JV scholarships (NNPC/Chevron, NNPC/Shell/SNEPCo, NNPC/Renaissance), including official-sounding anti-scam guidance pointing to this exact domain. Treat this corroboration as reasonably strong but not equivalent to a direct fetch of Chevron's or NNPC's own site confirming it — worth a final human check before demo, precisely because scholarship scams are common in Nigeria and this kind of shared-platform pattern is also what a convincing scam would look like.

programs.name: Jaiz Bank — MSME & Business Financing (Non-Interest)
programs.religion_note: Open to customers of all religions — a customer's faith is not a prerequisite for opening an account or accessing financing at Jaiz Bank. Some non-Muslim customers use non-interest banks specifically for their ethical/transparency model.
programs.benefit: Business financing structured as cost-plus-profit (Murabaha) rather than interest — e.g. the Special MSME Support Facility runs up to 1 year (micro enterprises) or up to 5 years (SMEs), with an optional moratorium. No fixed profit-rate percentage or loan ceiling was found published — amount and terms are set per business based on turnover and the specific product
programs.who_its_for: Registered Nigerian micro, small, and medium businesses wanting Sharia-compliant, non-interest financing — Nigeria's first full-fledged non-interest bank, open to applicants of any religion
eligibility: Business registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC)
Existing business/corporate bank account, generally with a track record as an active customer
Business should be profitable or show regular cash flow, with a clean Credit Bureau report (no unpaid defaults)
Typically expects some trading history (varies by product) — exact minimum not published
No religious requirement — open to all Nigerians
required_documents: Valid means of ID and proof of address
Collateral details, where applicable (bank has stated it is pursuing CBN approval for collateral-light, cash-flow-based SME lending in 2026)
programs.application_process: Visit a Jaiz Bank branch or contact Business Banking to discuss the MSME Support Facility, Murabaha working capital, or other non-interest financing products. No self-service online loan application form was found — a relationship officer assesses and structures the financing per business
programs.status: ongoing — general non-interest business financing; exact current MSME facility terms not independently confirmed
programs.source_url: jaizbankplc.com/business-banking (fetched directly, Sept 2026 — the specific /special-msme-support-facility/ sub-page 404'd on retry, may have moved); eligibility/documents corroborated via aggregator sukfin.com/knowledge/jaiz-bank/ (generic SME-lending guidance, not Jaiz-specific published criteria); non-Muslim accessibility confirmed via The Guardian Nigeria ('Jaiz Bank: Non-interest banking services not for Muslims only') and Legit.ng's coverage of CBN-approved non-interest banks
programs.notes: No profit-rate percentage is published anywhere found — non-interest banks don't quote a fixed 'interest rate' since financing is structured as cost-plus-profit (Murabaha/Ijara/etc). Get exact current figures from a branch before quoting a rate to users. apply_url points to Jaiz's own business banking page — do NOT use sukfin.com/apply/, which is an unrelated third-party loan marketplace, not Jaiz's official channel (same 'never show a fake Apply now' concern as the NELFUND entry).

programs.name: TAJBank — Business Financing (Non-Interest)
programs.religion_note: Non-interest banks in Nigeria, TAJBank included, do not require customers to be Muslim — a customer's religion is not a prerequisite for opening an account at any branch, per CBN-approved non-interest bank coverage. TAJBank itself does not publish a faith requirement.
programs.benefit: Non-interest financing across several structures: Cost Plus/Murabaha working capital, Murabaha import finance, Construction/Manufacturing (Istisna) finance, Lease (Ijara) finance, Agency (Wakalah) letters of credit, Bonds & Guarantees (Kafalah), and Partnership (Musharakah) funding. No fixed rate or ceiling published — sized to the business and product
programs.who_its_for: Registered Nigerian businesses needing working capital, import finance, equipment leasing, construction/manufacturing finance, or partnership funding — Nigeria's second full-fledged non-interest bank, open to applicants of any religion
eligibility: Business registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC)
Active business/corporate account, generally expected to be a TAJBank customer
Regular cash flow and a clean Credit Bureau report (no defaults)
Aggregator sources suggest 1-3 years' trading history is typically expected — not confirmed on TAJBank's own site
No religious requirement — open to all Nigerians
required_documents: Valid ID (passport, driver's license, voter's card) and proof of address
programs.application_process: Visit a TAJBank branch (Abuja HQ or Kano) or contact Business Banking to discuss the relevant non-interest financing product; no self-service online loan application form found — a loan adviser assesses the request and issues an offer letter if approved
programs.status: ongoing
programs.source_url: tajbank.com/business-banking/ (fetched directly, Sept 2026 — lists products but not eligibility/rates); eligibility/documents/process corroborated via aggregator sukfin.com/knowledge/taj-bank/ (generic guidance, not TAJBank-specific published criteria); non-Muslim accessibility per Legit.ng's CBN-approved non-interest bank coverage
programs.notes: Same caveat as Jaiz: no published profit-rate percentage, and eligibility/documents come from a third-party aggregator rather than TAJBank's own published criteria — verify directly with the bank before presenting specifics as confirmed. apply_url points to TAJBank's own business banking page — do NOT use sukfin.com/apply/, an unrelated broker site.

programs.name: Bank of Industry (BOI) — SME Financing
programs.religion_note: Not applicable — BOI is a conventional government development bank, not a non-interest/Sharia institution.
programs.benefit: Interest-based term loans and working capital, generally in the 9-12% per annum range on standard SME products (sector-specific programs, like GLOW for women-led businesses, can be lower — see separate entry). Amounts vary widely by programme and business size, from roughly ₦500,000 up to ₦1 billion; standard tenor is around 3-5 years with a 3-12 month moratorium option
programs.who_its_for: Registered Nigerian business entities across manufacturing and other value-chain sectors BOI supports
eligibility: Duly registered business entity (CAC) operating in a BOI-eligible sector
Viable business plan
At least 12 months of audited or management accounts
Good credit history
Collateral or a credible guarantor arrangement
required_documents: Valid means of ID (BVN, NIN, passport)
programs.application_process: Apply online via the relevant BOI programme portal (routed from boi.ng), which involves identity/BVN-NIN validation, CAC-based business verification, application completion, document upload, and assessment before disbursement
programs.status: ongoing — specific interest rate and loan ceiling depend on which BOI programme/sector window is current; recheck boi.ng before presenting exact figures
programs.source_url: boi.ng/smes/ (fetched directly, Sept 2026 — lists lending structure and tenor but not a single published rate); rate range and eligibility corroborated via nairacompare.ng and getoze.com aggregator coverage
programs.notes: BOI runs many overlapping sector/intervention windows (FGN MSME Intervention Program at fgnboimsmeinterventionloan.boi.ng, sector-specific funds, etc.) with different rates and ceilings — this entry is the general SME-financing umbrella, not one specific programme. Recheck boi.ng directly before quoting a specific rate or amount to a user.

programs.name: Bank of Industry — GLOW (Guaranteed Loans for Women)
programs.religion_note: Not applicable — BOI is a conventional government development bank, not a non-interest/Sharia institution.

programs.who_its_for: Women-owned and women-led Nigerian businesses in eligible sectors (manufacturing, ICT, e-commerce, creative industries, healthcare, education, renewable energy, waste management)
eligibility: Business owned or led by a woman
CAC business registration (RC or BN number)
Valid BVN and NIN
Operating in an eligible sector
required_documents: For limited companies: Certificate of Incorporation, tax clearance, audited accounts
programs.application_process: Register via the official BOI GLOW portal: identity validation (BVN/NIN), business verification via CAC number, application completion, document submission, assessment, then disbursement if approved
programs.status: ongoing as of Sept 2026
programs.source_url: boi.ng/sector/guaranteed-loans-for-women-glow/ (fetched directly, Sept 2026 — overview page, rate/ceiling not shown there); 7% rate, ceiling, and document list from withinnigeria.com (2026-09-18) explainer article
programs.notes: Strongest-sourced of the new bank/lender entries — 7% rate and ₦10-50m ceiling came from a specific, recently-published explainer rather than generic aggregator guidance, but neither figure was directly confirmed on BOI's own overview page, so still flagged needs_verification. Also fits the existing Women & Family category alongside GEEP MarketMoni.
